claim: RECRL perceives model-specific per-requirement difficulty and rewrites/optimizes hard requirements to improve RL training data utilization, achieving average Pass@1 gains of 1.23-5.62% over five SOTA curriculum-RL baselines across five LLMs and five benchmarks.
stance_target: existence of per-requirement difficulty modeling in code-LLM research
scope_conditions: 5 LLMs x 5 code generation benchmarks, curriculum RL training
quoted_support: RECRL achieves an average Pass@1 improvement of 1.23%-5.62% over all state-of-the-art baselines.

claim: RECRL's requirement-difficulty perception is a training-time RL curriculum mechanism operating on whole coding requirements/tasks, not a released evaluation benchmark, diagnostic subset, or unit-test-level (sub-task) partial-credit protocol.
stance_target: novelty of a released per-requirement benchmark/diagnostic artifact distinct from RL reward-shaping work
quoted_support: RECRL automatically perceives model-specific requirement difficulty, optimizes challenging requirements to improve training data utilization, and employs an adaptive curriculum sampling strategy
